searchText: <sophiagold0> re: **@jpwang** > yes, our understanding is that if you grind right before the fiat-shamir challenge at any place using the random oracle model in the interactive protocol, the grinding makes specific attacks on the randomness harder to find I want to return to this discussion. Do other zkVM teams using 32 bit fields think this approach is reasonable to reach 128 bits of security without changing the extension? <mratsim> re: **@kevaundray** > I think this adds a bit of complexity to the API, so I'm trying to see why this is being done. Do you plan to support guest programs in other languages such as go/c# etc? It's done because it allows hashing arbitrary sizes without holding everything in memory. For example this is used to implement HMAC and HKDF as used in EIP-2333. And it's also used in hash-to-curve to implement BLS signatures in the "expand-xmd" primitive <mratsim> See: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/constantine%2Fhash_to_curve%2Fh2c_hash_to_field.nim#L119 So zkvm will need the "update" for blob inputs and proving consensus / beam chain <mratsim> re: **@amvlasov** > If you are mainly talking about standarding interfaces for Reth/Revm, then why extern "C" at the first place? If you assume single e.g. Rust implementation for every language and C-header, then it's more about question if other languages codebases use or not use update approach on hashes I think only go doesn't use the update approach iirc.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<sophiagold0> re: **@jpwang**
> yes, our understanding is that if you grind right before the fiat-shamir challenge at any place using the random oracle model in the interactive protocol, the grinding makes specific attacks on the randomness harder to find
I want to return to this discussion. Do other zkVM teams using 32 bit fields think this approach is reasonable to reach 128 bits of security without changing the extension?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<mratsim> re: **@kevaundray**
> I think this adds a bit of complexity to the API, so I'm trying to see why this is being done.

Do you plan to support guest programs in other languages such as go/c# etc?
It's done because it allows hashing arbitrary sizes without holding everything in memory.

For example this is used to implement HMAC and HKDF as used in EIP-2333.

And it's also used in hash-to-curve to implement BLS signatures in the "expand-xmd" primitive

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<mratsim> See: https://github.com/mratsim/constantine/blob/master/constantine%2Fhash_to_curve%2Fh2c_hash_to_field.nim#L119

So zkvm will need the "update" for blob inputs and proving consensus / beam chain
